text_blocks.snippet: Scammers in Central Illinois frequently target residents using fake text messages, phone calls, and door-to-door repair schemes.

list.snippet:
Fake Law Enforcement & Court Calls: Scammers pose as local sheriffs or federal courts claiming you missed a jury duty date or have a warrant, demanding payment via Bitcoin, gift cards, or cash to avoid arrest. Local authorities remind residents that law enforcement never asks for money over the phone
.

DMV & Tollway Text Scams: Fraudulent texts claim you owe delinquent tolls or traffic fines and threaten license suspension if you do not click a link. The Illinois Secretary of State

confirms they do not send texts demanding immediate fine payments.

Police Text Scams: Con artists send SMS messages threatening vehicle conduct violations and driving authorization withdrawals. The Illinois State Police do not text citizens for immediate traffic penalties.

Storm & Garage Door Repair Schemes: Door-to-door contractors and "stormchasers" push quick fixes or complimentary inspections after severe weather. The Illinois Attorney General warns against upfront cash payments and signing immediate agreements.
Package Delivery Phishing: Texts pretending to be UPS or USPS claim a package cannot be delivered unless you pay a fee or update your address via a fake link.
Practice the pause: Stop and verify urgent claims instead of reacting under pressure.

Never click links:
Ignore unexpected text messages or emails regarding unpaid tolls, packages, or traffic citations.
Refuse cash and upfront pay: Never pay home repair contractors in full or in cash before work is completed and inspected.

Report fraud:
File complaints with the Federal Trade Commission or contact local law enforcement if you shared sensitive information.
